title: A Quantum-Inspired Approach to MaxCut Based on Sparse Walsh/Pauli-Correlation Encoding
authors: Cesar Augusto do Amaral, Marcos Vinicius Reballo, Marcus Ritt, Alexsandro Santos da Rosa Júnior, Fernando Augusto Caletti de Barros
abstract: We present a quantum-inspired Walsh/PCE solver for MaxCut based on sparse Pauli-correlation encodings. Instead of assigning one qubit or one variable to each graph vertex directly, the method represents relaxed binary variables through expectation values of diagonal Pauli/Walsh observables. These correlators are computed classically from sparse Walsh autocorrelations, producing a compact differentiable relaxation of the MaxCut objective. We evaluate the method on selected Gset instances, G1, G6, G12, and G18, and compare it with random search and tabu search over 10 independent seeds. The proposed model uses $801$ active parameters, corresponding to only $0.306\%$ of the full Walsh space over $18$ qubits. After a final bitflip local search, Walsh/PCE achieves approximation ratios of $0.99033 \pm 0.00226$ on G1, $0.95647 \pm 0.01604$ on G6, $0.96007 \pm 0.00951$ on G12, and $0.92964 \pm 0.02202$ on G18, outperforming both baselines on all tested instances. The method also yields the lowest average runtime in all cases. These results suggest that sparse Walsh/PCE representations provide an efficient quantum-inspired route for MaxCut and may be further extended to hardware-based estimation of Pauli/Walsh correlators.
summary: This paper proposes a quantum-inspired heuristic to solve the MaxCut problem using a sparse Walsh/PCE encoding. It reformulates the problem's objective function using expectation values of Pauli observables, calculated efficiently via sparse autocorrelation. The method demonstrates superior performance and speed compared to established classical search algorithms on benchmark graphs.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-hard MaxCut problem by formulating a quantum-inspired relaxation approach.
main_result: The proposed sparse Walsh/PCE method outperforms random search and tabu search on multiple benchmark instances, achieving high approximation ratios and the lowest average runtime.
method: It relaxes the MaxCut objective function by representing binary variables through expectation values of diagonal Pauli/Walsh observables, computed efficiently using sparse Walsh autocorrelations.
model_or_system: The problem is mapped to an Ising-type objective function, which is then approximated using a sparse Pauli-Correlation Encoding (PCE) framework based on Walsh operators.
key_observables: Approximation ratios (AR) on Gset instances (G1, G6, G12, G18), and average runtime ($	au$).
important_parameters: The method uses a sparse support of only 801 active parameters for 18 qubits, representing 0.306% of the full Walsh space.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the sparse Walsh/PCE representation provides a sufficient and efficient approximation for the MaxCut objective, followed by a final bitflip local search.

paper_structure: The paper develops from the general PCE framework to a specialized, computationally efficient, and structured Walsh-based encoding, detailing the mathematical formulation, presenting comparative results against classical heuristics, and discussing future hardware implementation.
why_interesting: While quantum-inspired, the core contribution lies in developing a highly efficient, differentiable classical simulation technique (sparse autocorrelation) to approximate a hard combinatorial optimization problem, which is valuable for developing novel classical solvers for quantum problems.
